result.result:
The budget tracker is built and covers all 11 requirements. The 18 unit tests pass, the browser test passes at 1280px and 375px, and type-check, lint and the production build come back clean. I haven't committed anything.

**How it works**
- **Exact amounts:** money is parsed from the text you type straight into whole cents and summed as whole numbers, so 0.1 + 0.2 shows 0.30. Amounts with more than two decimal places are rejected rather than rounded.
- **Main code:** the logic (validation, totals, filters, CSV, saving) is in `src/lib/money.ts` and `src/lib/budget.ts`. The interface is in `src/App.tsx`, and the donut chart is a hand-drawn SVG in `src/components/Donut.tsx`.
- **Budgets:** each category has one monthly limit that applies to every month. It shows a bar and "X left", or a red bar and "Over budget by X".
- **Months:** if you add a transaction dated in another month, the app switches to that month and tells you, so the entry doesn't seem to vanish.
- **Deleting:** asks you to confirm in the row itself ("Delete" / "Keep").
- **CSV export:** contains all of the selected month's transactions, even when filters are on. Quotes and commas are handled, and notes starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` get a leading `'` so spreadsheets don't run them as formulas.
- **Saving:** if browser storage is unreadable or corrupt the app starts with defaults instead of crashing, and if a save fails you see a warning banner.
- **New tooling:** I added `vitest` as a dev dependency, plus `npm test` (unit tests) and `npm run test:e2e` (browser tests) scripts.

**Fixed after looking at the screenshots**
- At 375px the header wrapped into a tall bar that stayed stuck to the top, and the Edit/Delete buttons cut transaction notes down to a few characters. On mobile the header is now compact and doesn't stick, the three totals sit in one row, and the buttons moved under the amount.
- The colour picker for a new category defaulted to the same violet as Fun. It now picks a colour no category is using yet.

**What I tested and how**
- **Unit tests (`npm test`, 18 passing):**
  - Reading amounts: decimals, thousands separators, and rejecting empty, zero, negative, non-numeric, too many decimals and too large.
  - 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30.
  - Number formatting.
  - Validation messages, including a missing date, impossible dates like Feb 30 and leap years.
  - Category names: empty or duplicate rejected.
  - Month switching across year boundaries.
  - Picking the selected month's transactions.
  - Totals and per-category spending.
  - Every filter combination and case-insensitive search.
  - Budget percentages and the over-budget point.
  - CSV quoting and the formula guard.
  - Saving and reloading, falling back on corrupt data, and a failed save.
- **Browser test (`npx playwright test`, `e2e/budget.spec.ts`):** one script clicks through everything in real Chrome, once at 1280×900 and once at 375×812:
  - Every validation message.
  - Adding income and expenses, including 0.1 + 0.2 showing 0.30, and checking all three totals.
  - Editing, cancelling a delete, then deleting.
  - Adding a custom category, including the empty-name and duplicate-name errors, and checking its colour appears in the chart.
  - Setting a budget under the limit, then over it, and checking the bar turns red.
  - Rejecting a zero budget, then clearing a budget.
  - Each filter, search, and "Clear filters".
  - Downloading the CSV and checking its contents.
  - The previous/next/today buttons, with totals, chart and list emptying for a month with no data.
  - Adding into another month and checking the app switches to it.
  - Hovering the chart ring and legend.
  - No sideways scrolling.
  - Reloading the page and checking transactions, the custom category and budgets are still there.
- **Visual check:** I saved full-page screenshots at both sizes and looked at them myself, which is how I found the mobile layout problems above.

I've moved "Clear filters" into the filter row and changed the income colour to teal (`#0d7f80`). Both browser tests (1280px and 375px) and all 18 unit tests pass.

- **Clear filters:** the button now sits right of the search box. On desktop it's in the same row as the two dropdowns; on mobile it shares the second row with the search box. It's always there but greyed out until a filter is set, and one click resets category, type and search. This replaces the old link that only appeared below the filters.
- **Income colour:** the Income total and the `+` amounts in the list are teal. I picked a darker teal so it stays easy to read on white.

**What I checked**
- **Existing tests:** `npm test` (18 unit tests) and `npx playwright test` (the full walkthrough of every requirement at 1280×900 and 375×812) both pass. The type-check is also clean.
- **Clear filters, new browser checks at both sizes:**
  - The button is disabled when no filters are set.
  - It sits level with the search box, to its right, and fits on screen at 375px.
  - It's enabled once type, category and search are all set.
  - One click shows all 6 rows again, empties all three fields and disables the button again.
- **Teal, new browser checks at both sizes:** the Income total and the Salary row amount both measure `rgb(13, 127, 128)` in the browser.
- **Screenshots:** I looked at them at both sizes. The new button fits neatly on desktop and on mobile, and the teal shows on the income figures.
  - On desktop, only the Salary amount was visible in teal. The page header covered the Income total in the full-page capture, a screenshot quirk. The colour check above covers that figure.

Recurring transactions are working. All 41 unit tests pass, and all 4 browser tests pass: the original app walkthrough and the new recurring one, each at 1280px and 375px. Lint and the production build are clean, and I haven't committed anything.

**How it works**
- **Repeat monthly:** a checkbox in the add/edit form. The hint underneath says when it will repeat, for example "every later month on the 31st (or the last day in shorter months)".
- **Copies are real transactions:** each month's copy is a normal transaction, so it counts in totals, the chart, budgets and CSV export. Repeating rows show a "↻ Monthly" badge.
- **No duplicates:** each repeating transaction remembers the last month it has filled in. Opening a later month fills in every month up to it, including any you skipped, and never fills a month twice. Reopening a month or reloading adds nothing, and a single copy you delete stays deleted.
- **Short months:** the 31st becomes the 30th, the 28th, or the 29th in leap years.
- **Recurring screen:** a new tab next to "Overview" with an active-count badge. It lists every repeating transaction with its day, amount, months covered, and Active or Stopped.
  - "Stop…" lets you pick the first month it should no longer appear in, and tells you what happens: "May 2026 and earlier stay as they are. 21 transactions from June 2026 on will be removed."
  - A stopped one can be stopped earlier, but not pushed later.

**Choices I made where the spec was open**
- **Editing a copy that still repeats:** the change applies to that month and all later months; earlier months keep their old values. Moving it to a different month is blocked with a clear message. You can still change the day.
- **Unticking "Repeat monthly" while editing:** this copy is kept as a one-off and the repeat stops from that month on.
- **Ticking it on an existing one-off:** that transaction becomes the first month of a new repeating transaction.
- **Stopping from the very first month:** the repeating transaction and all its copies are removed, so it leaves the list.
- **Export button moved on mobile:** on mobile, "Export CSV" moved from the header into the Transactions card to make room for the tabs. On desktop it's still in the header.

The logic is in `src/lib/recurring.ts` and the new screen is `src/components/RecurringScreen.tsx`. Data saved before this change still loads.

**What I tested and how**
- **Unit tests (`npm test`, 41 total, 23 new in `src/lib/recurring.test.ts`):**
  - Month lengths and leap years, and moving the 29th, 30th and 31st to the last day of shorter months.
  - Filling in months, including jumps that skip months.
  - Opening the same or an earlier month again changes nothing.
  - Nothing appears before the start month, and deleted copies don't come back.
  - Stopping from a chosen month leaves earlier months exactly as they were, and nothing reappears in later months.
  - Stopping only moves earlier, never later, and stopping from the first month removes everything.
  - Every edit case: one-off to repeating, editing a copy (earlier months untouched), moving to another month (blocked), and unticking repeat.
  - Saving and loading, malformed saved data, and data saved before this feature.
- **Browser test (`e2e/recurring.spec.ts`, real Chrome at 1280×900 and 375×812), clicking through:**
  - Adding repeating and one-off transactions, and checking the badges and the hint text.
  - Stepping through the months: Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30.
  - Going back, reloading, and checking the saved data has no duplicates.
  - Jumping to Feb 2028: the gap months are filled and the date is the 29th.
  - Editing a copy, including the different-month error, with earlier months unchanged.
  - Deleting one copy and checking it stays gone.
  - The Recurring screen's contents.
  - Stopping from June 2026: the summary text, months before untouched, none from June on, still stopped after a reload.
  - The "already stops from June 2026" error when choosing a later month.
  - Unticking repeat while editing.
  - Stopping from the first month.
  - Turning a one-off into a repeating transaction.
  - No sideways scrolling on either screen.
- **Regression:** the original `e2e/budget.spec.ts` walkthrough of all 11 requirements still passes at both sizes.
- **Visual check:** I looked at screenshots of the Overview, the Recurring list and the Stop panel at both sizes, and found nothing to fix.
